questions.q: What makes something an actual freshness SLA rather than just a vague goal?
options: It's a specific, checkable claim about maximum staleness, like "never more than 15 minutes old"
Using the phrase "near real-time" in the requirements document
Any dashboard that refreshes automatically counts as meeting an SLA
Freshness SLAs cannot be tested or measured by definition
questions.explain: "Near real-time" can't be tested; a specific number like "no more than 15 minutes stale" can.

questions.q: Why does Lesson 5's processing model choice matter for what freshness SLA is achievable?
options: The batch/streaming/hybrid choice mechanically caps what freshness is achievable before any pipeline code is written
The processing model has no relationship to achievable freshness
Freshness SLAs are decided entirely independently of any architecture
Batch processing always achieves better freshness than streaming
questions.explain: You cannot promise a 5-minute SLA on top of a nightly batch job — the processing model already decided the ceiling.

questions.q: What does this lesson say is the real trade-off behind lower latency freshness?
options: Lower latency generally requires compute running continuously, which costs more than a batch job that spins up once and shuts down
Lower latency always costs less than higher latency
There is no cost difference between streaming and batch freshness
Freshness has no relationship to compute cost at all
questions.explain: An always-on streaming pipeline costs differently than a batch job that runs once a night and goes idle.

questions.q: How is freshness actually measured, end to end, according to this lesson?
options: As the gap between when an event happened and when it became queryable — available_at minus event_time
By counting the total number of rows in a table
Freshness cannot be measured in practice
By how many dashboards reference the data
questions.explain: The metric is available_at minus event_time — the real end-to-end lag, not an assumption.

questions.q: What role does watermarking play in a freshness SLA, per this lesson's reference to Fabric Lesson 33?
options: It decides how long a streaming pipeline waits for late-arriving data before finalizing a window, trading freshness against completeness
Watermarking has no connection to freshness at all
Watermarking guarantees zero staleness in every case
Watermarking only applies to nightly batch jobs
questions.explain: A tighter watermark hits the SLA sooner but risks finalizing before all data arrives; a looser one is more complete but slower.
